The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 3.8% on October 16, 2026, its eighth straight losing session and its longest run since 2008. The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.5% on the same date, and tech stocks lost more than a trillion dollars in value.

24/7 Wall Street

The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) tracks a similar index. It fell 4.14% to $493.39. It closed at $589.45 on October 6, so it is now down about 16% since then and sits about 25% below its 52-week high of $655.95. Equipment Makers Fell With Chip Designers

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) fell 5.95%. Intel lost 5.79%, Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) 5.63%, Marvell Technology 5.56% and Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) 4.52%. Three chip equipment makers also fell. KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) dropped 5.00%, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) 4.87% and Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) 4.82%.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) slid only 1.43%. Chip designers, memory makers and equipment makers all fell on the same day, which suggests investors doubt the spending cycle that pays all of them.

Bearish investors accumulated roughly $32 billion in paper profits over seven days as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped over 12% during an eight-session slump.

Broad market indexes felt the ripple effect, with the S&P 500 on track for its worst weekly decline since June and the Nasdaq 100 sliding 5%.

Short sellers betting against AI cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. netted more than $1 billion in mark-to-market profits following distressed debt signals and rising default risks.

Short sellers have bagged a multi-billion-dollar payday amid a retreat in semiconductor stocks driven by CoreWeave's debt concerns.

Short sellers recorded $32 billion in gross paper profits over a seven-day span as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeted more than 12%, S3 data showed, as quoted by Bloomberg.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

The sector benchmark, widely known as the SOX, extended its slump to eight consecutive trading days on Friday, putting it on pace to mirror its longest losing streak since 2006.

Market Anxiety Around AI Spending Persist

The recent decline reflects growing market anxiety about elevated interest rates, lofty tech valuations, and the massive AI capital expenditures.

The selloff in chips has spilled over into broader equity benchmarks, setting the S&P 500 up for a 1.7% weekly decline, its steepest since June, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 dropped 5% in the week ending October 16.

Out of the 30 companies comprising the SOX index, 20 have lost over 10% of their value since the downturn began. Coherent Corp.(COHR) led the losses with a dive of nearly 30%.

"The run up in chips was very aggressive so invariably there was going to be some consolidation or pull back," Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management told Bloomberg.

CoreWeave Shorts Yield Massive Returns

Short sellers targeting CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV), an AI-focused cloud computing firm, logged over $1 billion in gains as the company's equity dropped more than 20% over the week.

CoreWeave's debt instruments slipped into distressed territory, with credit-default swaps indicating a greater than 50% likelihood of default over the next five years.S3 data noted that a portion of the short interest in CoreWeave stems from convertible bond arbitrage strategies rather than purely directional bearish bets.

"CoreWeave specifically is going to need a new story," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager of the Rational Equity Armor Fund told Bloomberg. "It's going to need time to digest this new reality."

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) dropped 1.2%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) eased 0.5%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) fell 2.5% on Friday.

Why Does VRTX Catch Our Eye?

title: Stocks Up Pre-Bell as Traders Parse President Trump's Latest Comments on Iran War
detail:
PREMIUM
Stocks Up Pre-Bell as Traders Parse President Trump's Latest Comments on Iran War
MT Newswires
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 7:02 AM CDT 3 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^NDX
stock trading market equity wall street -Shutterstock

The benchmark US stock measures were pointing higher before the open Friday as traders assess President Donald Trump's latest comments on the war with Iran.

The S&P 500 edged up 0.1%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.3% in premarket activity, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.1%. Equity markets finished the previous trading session in the green.

In an interview with Newsmax on Thursday, Trump said he isn't considering sending ground troops into Iran.

Trump's comments came after CNN reported, citing sources, that the US military has developed plans that include the potential use of a so-called "mother of all bombs" to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites.

"The mother of all bombs is not nuclear," Trump said in the Newsmax interview. "This is just an extremely large bomb."

Trump said the US may have to strike Iran's Pickaxe mountain, a suspected nuclear site, but he doesn't see ground troops being deployed for such an operation, Newsmax reported. The US leader also said Iran is negotiating with Washington and expressed confidence that the war in the Middle East "will be over very soon."

West Texas Intermediate crude oil decreased 0.6% to $97.39 a barrel early Friday, while Brent dipped 0.2% to $105.73.

The International Energy Agency on Thursday outlined plans to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel "as soon as possible" as part of its efforts to address a global supply crunch. In March, the agency agreed to release a record 400 million barrels of oil in a bid to stem crude prices and address supply disruptions triggered by the Middle East conflict.

Treasury yields were mixed, with the two-year rate retreating 0.5 basis points to 4.75% while the 10-year rate gained 1.3 basis points to 5.1%.

Government data showed Thursday producer prices jumped at the fastest pace in more than four years in September amid a surge in energy costs, a day after a report showed consumer inflation also accelerated last month.

Retail sales growth exceeded expectations in September as outlays at gas stations increased amid elevated fuel prices, the Census Bureau reported Thursday.

"With core inflation running at 2.6% year-on-year and oil prices remaining elevated, which increases the risk that price pressures spread to other categories, the (Federal Reserve) likely will not be able to remain on the sidelines for much longer," TD Economics Economist Admir Kolaj said in a Thursday note.

Despite the hot inflation reports, markets are currently pricing in an 85% probability that the Fed will keep its benchmark rate steady later this month, up from 72% on Thursday, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The remaining odds are in favor of a 25-basis-point hike.

Friday's economic calendar has the import and export prices report for September, followed by the industrial production report for the same month and the weekly Baker Hughes oil-and-gas rig count.

Travelers (TRV), Truist Financial (TFC), M&T Bank (MTB), Citizens Financial (CFG) and Regions Financial (RF) report their latest financial results before the bell.

Shares of Tesla (TSLA) jumped 4.3% pre-bell after the electric vehicle manufacturer unveiled its new Roadster car capable of flight using cold-gas thrusters. Nike (NKE) added 0.9% after closing the previous session with an increase of 5.2%.

J.B. Hunt Transport Services (JBHT) was down 1.3% as its third-quarter operating income as a percentage of revenue declined year over year.

Spot gold inclined 0.8% to $4,203 per troy ounce, while bitcoin traded down 0.3% at $82,080.
